 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 27.11.2018 passed in MVC No.7517/2017 by the Chief Judge, Court of small causes, member MACT at Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the respondent-BMTC therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. On 22.11.2017, the petitioner was riding a moped bearing No.KA-05-JN-0945 near Aswini Bar,
Nayandahalli, Mysore Road, Bengaluru, he met with an accident at about 11.30 a.m. when a BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-2044 came and dashed against him.

The tribunal on the ground that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the BMTC bus has awarded a sum of Rs.9,00,000/- to the petitioner with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the same, the present petition is filed.
4. The appeal is filed on the grounds that the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the injured petitioner and also that the compensation granted is excessive.

5. Based on the evidence let in and on the strength that the charge-sheet has been filed against the driver of the bus, the tribunal has come to the conclusion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the BMTC bus.
The respondent is not in a position to show where and how the tribunal has erred in coming to such a conclusion.

The FIR, complaint, sketch, mahazar,
charge-sheet and the oral and documentary evidence in the case shows the negligence on part of the driver of the BMTC Bus.
As there is no cogent reasons given by the respondents in the given appeal I am not inclined to interfere with the well reasoned order of the tribunal in so far as it relates to negligence.

6. In respect of the compensation awarded the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Abanded laceration 5cm x 3. c.m.
2. abrasion 1 x 1 c.m. base of right elbow.
3. Abrasion 3 x 2 c.m. front of right elbow.
4. grazed abrasion over right hip 10 x 1 c.m.
5. Degloving injury of right hip.
6. Pelvis bone fractured.

7. left side peumothorax.
The same are grievous in nature.
The petitioner was inpatient for a period of 19 days.
She was aged 24 years and based on the evidence let in the tribunal has considered the whole body disability at 15%.
The Accident is of the year 2017.
The tribunal has taken the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.7,000/- whereas, the same fixed by Lok Adalat chart is on the higher side.

Based on the same,
loss of income during the later period and future loss of earning due to disability have been calculated by the tribunal and I do not see any reason to reduce the same.
With regard to pain and sufferings, medical expenses, food and nourishment and loss of amenities the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/-, Rs.5,47,000/- Rs.25,000/- and Rs.40,000/- respectively.
I do not see any reason to reduce the same and deemed the same to be just and reasonable.
7. For the aforementioned reasons the appeal being devoid of merits is hereby dismissed.
The amount in deposit shall stand transferred to the tribunal for disbursement.
